back_translation: These are the names of the tribes: At the northern frontier, Dan shall have one portion, with its border running along the road of Hethlon to Lebo-hamath, through Hazar-enan on the border of Damascus, with Hamath to the north, extending from the east side to the west side.
Asher shall have one portion bordering the territory of Dan from east to west.
Naphtali shall have one portion bordering the territory of Asher from east to west.
Manasseh shall have one portion bordering the territory of Naphtali from east to west.
Ephraim shall have one portion bordering the territory of Manasseh from east to west.
Reuben shall have one portion bordering the territory of Ephraim from east to west.
Judah shall have one portion bordering the territory of Reuben from east to west.
Bordering the territory of Judah, from east to west, shall be the district you set apart, 25,000 cubits wide and as long as a tribal portion from east to west; in its center shall be the sanctuary.
The district you set apart to the LORD shall be 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide.

This holy district shall belong to the priests: 25,000 cubits long on the north, 10,000 cubits wide on the west, 10,000 cubits wide on the east, and 25,000 cubits long on the south; in its center shall be the sanctuary of the LORD.
It shall be for the consecrated priests, the descendants of Zadok, who kept My charge and did not go astray as the Levites did when the Israelites went astray.
It shall be a special set-apart portion for them, taken from the set-apart district of the land, a most holy portion, adjacent to the territory of the Levites.
Bordering the territory of the priests, the Levites shall have an area 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide; the whole length 25,000 and the width 10,000.
They must not sell or exchange any of it, and they must not transfer this best part of the land, for it is holy to the LORD.
The remaining 5,000 cubits in width along the 25,000 shall be for common use by the city, for dwellings and pastureland, with the city in its center.
These shall be its measurements: the north side 4,500 cubits, the south side 4,500, the east side 4,500, and the west side 4,500.
The pastureland of the city shall extend 250 cubits to the north, 250 to the south, 250 to the east, and 250 to the west.
The rest of the length alongside the holy district shall be 10,000 cubits on the east and 10,000 on the west; its produce shall be food for the workers of the city.
The workers of the city who cultivate it shall come from all the tribes of Israel.
The entire set-apart district shall be a square of 25,000 by 25,000 cubits; you shall set apart the holy district together with the city property.

The remaining area on both sides of the holy district and the city property shall belong to the prince; he shall hold the land alongside the tribal portions, extending east from the 25,000 to the eastern border and west from the 25,000 to the western border; in its center shall be the holy district and the sanctuary of the temple.
So the Levites' property and the city's property shall lie in the center of the area belonging to the prince—the area between the borders of Judah and Benjamin shall be the prince's.
As for the rest of the tribes: Benjamin shall have one portion extending from east to west.
Simeon shall have one portion bordering the territory of Benjamin from east to west.
Issachar shall have one portion bordering the territory of Simeon from east to west.
Zebulun shall have one portion bordering the territory of Issachar from east to west.
Gad shall have one portion bordering the territory of Zebulun from east to west.
The southern border of Gad shall run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, then along the Brook of Egypt out to the Great Sea.
This is the land you shall allot as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel, and these are their portions, declares the Lord GOD.
These are the exits of the city: On the north side, which shall be 4,500 cubits long,
the gates of the city shall be named after the tribes of Israel. On the north there shall be three gates: the gate of Reuben, the gate of Judah, and the gate of Levi.
On the east side, 4,500 cubits long, three gates: the gate of Joseph, the gate of Benjamin, and the gate of Dan.
On the south side, 4,500 cubits long, three gates: the gate of Simeon, the gate of Issachar, and the gate of Zebulun.
On the west side, 4,500 cubits long, three gates: the gate of Gad, the gate of Asher, and the gate of Naphtali.
The perimeter of the city shall be 18,000 cubits, and from that day on the name of the city shall be: 'Yahweh-Shammah' (THE LORD IS THERE).
